review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed response inspection to submission; includes coordinator/tool latency, not isolated human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally represent the indices from col through n-1 as a finite search domain. Mark exactly the first index whose absolute active-column value is maximal: its value must be at least every candidate value and strictly greater than every earlier candidate value having a smaller index. Use Grover-style search only to propose that unique pivot index.

Encode the current column index, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 values rows[i][col]. A reversible oracle would need exact implementations of Python-compatible absolute value, binary64 comparison, equality, and first-index tie handling. The representation, coherent loading method, handling of signed zero and intermediate nonfinite values, ancilla cleanup, and gate costs remain unresolved.

Measure a candidate index and classically verify that it equals Python's first-index argmax under abs(rows[i][col]). If verification or quantum search fails, execute the original classical max operation. After verification, retain the exact zero-pivot check, row swap, elimination, back substitution, overflow behavior, and output construction unchanged.
Inputs are validated finite binary64 values, but the pivot oracle would consume dynamically updated elimination state.

binding.rationale: Unlike the first draft, this formulation explicitly requires the candidate magnitude to be at least every candidate magnitude and strictly greater than each earlier-indexed candidate magnitude. Transcribe those exact >= and > quantifiers on the active indices; the stored values are absolute pivot magnitudes. Every candidate includes the candidate itself; earlier candidates are explicitly smaller indices. The response acknowledges unresolved intermediate nonfinite handling but supplies no operational domain guard, so the literal predicate is checked with guard True. This examines the proposed unique-marker relation only, not a completed oracle or the whole hybrid plan. The explicit classical verification/fallback is recorded in the prose anchors and is not disproved or executed by this local checker.

interpretations.meaning: Candidate magnitude is >= every active candidate magnitude and > every earlier active magnitude, exactly as stated.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices) and all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i)
